schema.name: isikdere_phase1_dataset
schema.description: Single consolidated Phase-1 reference state for the coupled hydro-mechanical PINN slope-stability model of the Isikdere lignite open pit. All values strict SI. Supersedes phase1_reference_state.json and step_1_2_1_3_adopted_parameters.json, both of which contain values corrected here (see conflicts_resolved).
schema.units: m, s, Pa, kg/m^3, K in m/s, alpha in 1/m and 1/Pa, angles in degrees unless the key ends _rad
schema.primary_source: Ulusay, R., Ekmekci, M., Tuncay, E. & Hasancebi, N. (2014). Improvement of slope stability based on integrated geotechnical evaluations and hydrogeological conceptualisation at a lignite open pit. Engineering Geology 181, 261-280. DOI 10.1016/j.enggeo.2014.08.005

sources_disagree: Phase1_Reference_State.docx / phase1_reference_state.json: marl 478 MPa (MR=400)
Step_1_2_1_3 master sheet: marl 208.9 MPa (MR=175)
conflicts_resolved.reason: Hoek & Diederichs (2006) tabulate MR = 150-200 for marls. MR = 400 is twice the published upper bound. 478 MPa is retained as the upper sensitivity case only. Coal (93.4) and tuffite (32.3) agree between sources to rounding.

sources_disagree: Ulusay et al. text + Step 1.1 SI sheet: 0.056 m3/day/m = 6.48e-7 m3/s/m
Fig. 9 plotted curve: 0.56 m3/day/m = 6.48e-6 m3/s/m
conflicts_resolved.reason: Summing q(t)=0.56/sqrt(t) over 30 days gives 5.368 m3/m, matching the paper's own published cumulative of 5.37 to 3 s.f. The 0.056 version gives 0.537 - ten times too small. The text carries a typographic error; the figure is right. This is a factor-of-ten error in a boundary condition - it would have invalidated every transient result.

sources_disagree: Phase1_Reference_State.docx: roadmap placeholders (underclay 0.07/0.43/1.0/1.23)
Step_1_2_1_3 master sheet: Rosetta3-computed + porosity-tied analogs
conflicts_resolved.reason: Soils are now computed from site grain-size + dry bulk density with Rosetta3 (Tier A, with 1-sigma bands). Rock analogs are porosity-tied via theta_s = 0.9*n0 using each stratum's OWN porosity, which the placeholders did not do - the placeholder set gave the weak-zone marl and tuffite the same theta_s as the marl.

sources_disagree: phase1_reference_state.json: weak-zone 0.427 (copied from marl), tuffite 0.400 (estimate)
phase relation from each stratum's own gamma and Gs: 0.350 and 0.413
conflicts_resolved.resolution: ADOPTED 0.3499 (weak-zone marl) and 0.4128 (tuffite), recomputed from n0 = 1 - gamma_dry/(gamma_w*Gs).
conflicts_resolved.reason: Both strata have their own reported unit weight (16.9 and 14.4 kN/m3). There was no reason to inherit the marl's porosity or to estimate. n0 drives the Kozeny-Carman permeability feedback, so a 0.077 error in the weak zone - the stratum that actually fails - propagates straight into the coupled loop.

sources_disagree: Phase1_Reference_State.docx: 0.40
Step_1_3 master sheet: 0.35
conflicts_resolved.reason: Both are inside the literature band for stiff CL-CH clay. 0.35 is the value used in the sheet that actually derived the elastic tensor, so the Lame constants shipped here are self-consistent with it. Note K0 = nu/(1-nu) differs by 0.13 between the two, which matters for the geostatic initial condition in Step 2.3 - keep it in the Step 6.2 sweep.

sources_disagree: nondim.py / Step_1_6 doc: 1e9 Pa
Step_1_2_1_3 sheet recommendation: ~1e8 Pa
conflicts_resolved.resolution: ADOPTED 1e8 Pa; U_ref becomes 1.70 m (was 0.17 m).
conflicts_resolved.reason: No stratum in the model is as stiff as 1 GPa - the adopted moduli run 8e6 to 2.09e8 Pa. Scaling displacement by a modulus an order above the real material leaves u* far below O(1), which is the thing the exercise exists to prevent. ACTION: update nondim.py line E_ref: float = 1.0e9 -> 1.0e8.

sources_disagree: figure as printed: Cv reads 6-8% for most wells
paper text: Cv below 5% in the great majority, never above 10%
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Series are plotted against opposite axes to their titles. Blue bars = Cv on the right axis; red line = average head on the left. Corrected values shipped.
conflicts_resolved.reason: Read as corrected, the red line reproduces the Fig.7 average heads almost exactly (GK.10 = 112, GK.11 = 226) and Cv comes out 0.05-8.4%, matching the text.

sources_disagree: labels as printed: ascending sigma_n top-to-bottom
physics: shear strength must increase with normal stress
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Mapping reversed - highest curve = 260 kPa. Corrected envelope shipped.
conflicts_resolved.reason: The corrected mapping gives phi_peak = 28.8 deg and phi_res = 15.1 deg, matching Table 3a row 1 (27.9 / 14.4) within a degree. The printed order implies phi_peak = 65 deg at 68 kPa, which is impossible.

sources_disagree: figure prints F = 1.250
text says flattening to 20 deg achieves F = 1.3
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Benchmark against 1.250 at 20 deg. The 18-deg case (1.346) is the only one that actually clears 1.3.

sources_disagree: packer tests: K = 0.1-0.5 m/day over the seam thickness
Fig. 10a curve fit: w = T/S = 1850 m2/day, which with S = 3e-5 gives T = 0.056 m2/day
conflicts_resolved.resolution: UNRESOLVED - deliberately. Both values are carried in the dataset.
conflicts_resolved.reason: For any plausible seam thickness (1-30 m) the packer K implies T two orders above the fitted value. Either the plotted curves assume a much larger S or a much smaller K. This is a genuine ambiguity in the source, not a digitisation artefact. Pick one, justify it in the methodology, and show the other as a sensitivity case. Do not let the code pick silently.

marl_sekkoy.label: Marl (Sekkoy Fm.)
marl_sekkoy.K_s_basis: ~0 Lugeon, no water intake; numerical aquitard floor
marl_sekkoy.vg_basis: Carsel & Parrish (1988) silty-clay alpha; theta_s = 0.9*n0; n raised 1.09->1.20 for autodiff smoothness

marl_weakzone.label: Weak-zone marl (Sekkoy Fm.)
marl_weakzone.vg_basis: marl analog, identical alpha/n; theta_s = 0.9*n0 from its own porosity

coal.label: Coal seam (lignite)
coal.K_s_basis: 0.1-0.5 m/day (~5 Lu, 423 packer tests); midpoint 0.25 m/day
coal.vg_basis: single-porosity equivalent continuum for fractured medium (Peters & Klavetter 1988); theta_s = fracture porosity ~0.15, RQD ~70%

tuffite.label: Tuffite (Yatagan Fm.)
tuffite.vg_basis: nonwelded-pyroclastic analog (Flint 2003); theta_s = 0.9*n0. LEAST-CONSTRAINED SWCC in the set

underclay.label: Underclay (Turgut Fm.)
underclay.Gs_source: paper mean (printed 2.44-25.7 is a typo for 2.44-2.57)
underclay.K_s_basis: reported impervious; floor value. Rosetta3 plausibility estimate 5.6e-7 m/s
underclay.vg_basis: Rosetta3 model 3, SSC + dry BD 1.544 g/cm3 (Zhang & Schaap 2017)

slope_debris.label: Slope debris
slope_debris.K_s_basis: NOT TESTED. Rosetta3 estimate 1.2e-6 m/s adopted so the rainfall Neumann BC has a receiving medium; sensitivity-critical
slope_debris.vg_basis: Rosetta3 model 3, SSC + dry BD 1.347 g/cm3

hoek_brown_mc_equivalents.note: Equivalent c, phi from the Hoek (2002) closed-form MC linearisation over 0 <= sig3' <= sig3max. These describe the INTACT ROCK-MASS envelope and are far stronger than the discontinuity strengths that govern the real bedding-controlled failures. Use these ONLY for the GHB-vs-MC contrast (Step 5.2); the MC-SSR sweep (Step 5.1) uses mc_strength.design_pair. c and phi are not material constants here - they depend entirely on the confining range fitted.

design_pair.basis: Table 3a lubricated residual AND back-analysis of INS-2/INS-3 at F=1; THIS is the pair to reduce in the MC-SSR sweep (Step 5.1)

back_analysis.note: two Fig.14a envelopes closest at c=1 kPa; digitised mean phi 15.05 deg
Fig.14b envelopes intersect at c=7.1 kPa, phi=16.6 deg, inside the RESIDUAL box

geometry.geometry_confidence: GRADE C: digitised from small rasters with vertical exaggeration. +/-10 m vertical, +/-10 m horizontal. Adequate to size the collocation domain and place BCs; NOT adequate for a publishable SSR result. Re-digitise Fig.19 from the vector PDF before final runs.

piezometric_heads_masl.note: coal-seam heads are fault-compartmentalised; GK.13/GKD1/GK.17/GK.18 sit in separate low compartments and should not be averaged with the rest

steady_state_justification.conclusion: Cv < 5% in 20 of 23 wells over the 2010-2011 monitoring year -> the pre-excavation head field is effectively steady. Use it as the steady-state initial condition; introduce transience only via excavation.

seepage_face_flux.model: q(t) = q1 / sqrt(t)  (Nguyen & Raudkivi 1982 seepage-face solution)
seepage_face_flux.validation: reconstructed cumulative matches the published 5.37 to 3 s.f.
seepage_face_flux.WARNING: the paper's text prints q1 = 0.056, which is a factor-of-ten typo. The 0.056 value propagated into the Step 1.1 SI sheet (6.48e-7 m3/s/m). USE 6.481e-6 m3/s/m.

drawdown_analytic.use: Phase-5 validation target for the Richards solver; NOT a training label
drawdown_analytic.WARNING: w = T/S = 1850 m2/day with the paper's S = 3e-5 implies T = 0.056 m2/day, roughly two orders below the packer-test coal K for any plausible seam thickness. Either the figure uses a larger S or a smaller K. State which you adopt in the methodology - do not resolve it silently.

rainfall.status: NOT YET ACQUIRED - blocking for Phase 2
rainfall.reason: INS-2 and INS-3 followed a heavy-rainfall week; the surface Neumann flux is the forcing the whole transient case rests on

lem_factors_of_safety.mechanism: compound: debris + weak zone + marl, bedding-following
compound along the underclay; most critical northern section
compound through overburden along Sekkoy bedding
compound through overburden + coal along underclay; confined coal aquifer degrades stability

lem_factors_of_safety.note: text claims 1.3 here; benchmark against the printed 1.250

lem_factors_of_safety.mechanism: multi-planar, Fault 17 controlled; most critical section in the pit

validation.fos_grade: GRADE A: values printed on Fig.19 a-e, cross-checked against Section 8.2.2 text. Where both exist, benchmark against the figure value (3 d.p.) not the text value (2 d.p.).

cheapest_first_benchmark.target: SSR on the INS-1 profile with c = 1 kPa, phi = 15 deg must return F = 1.00
cheapest_first_benchmark.why: single back-analysed section, no coupling required; run it before any pit section

shear_envelope_digitised.source: Fig. 11, normal-stress mapping CORRECTED (highest curve = 260 kPa)
shear_envelope_digitised.note: constrained (c=0) fits are the meaningful ones; the unconstrained regression returns a physically meaningless negative cohesion and is the error bar, not the result

scale_justification.T_ref: 1 day - the transient rainfall response is the phenomenon of interest
scale_justification.H_ref: 165 m, the largest suction head in the domain. psi over the initial condition spans -3 to -161 m, so this puts psi* in [-1, 0]: the field fills the network's output range without saturating the activation. The original 30 m (max piezometric head above the coal seam) gave psi* down to -5.4.
scale_justification.E_ref: 1e8 Pa, a MARL scale. u* = u/U_ref = E_ref/E_actual, so E_ref must sit within about an order of magnitude of the strata that actually deform. Adopted rock-mass moduli are Mk 2.09e8, Mk_d 3.81e7 and Tm 4.26e9 Pa -- a span of 112x, so no single E_ref puts all three within an order. Tm is excluded: it is the crystallised limestone basement, effectively rigid, and small u* there is physically correct rather than a scaling failure; the failure mechanism runs through the marls. The Mk/Mk_d geometric mean is 8.9e7, i.e. the adopted 1e8. The original 1e9 gave u* = 26 for Mk_d, stiffer than every deforming stratum in the model.

nondimensionalisation.caveat: The mechanical residual is balanced (all three groups O(1)). The Richards residual is NOT: Pi_R_diff ~ 3e-6 with T_ref = 1 day. That is physically correct - the pit's diffusive timescale is ~916 years - not an error. Keep T_ref = 1 day and apply explicit per-residual normalisation in the loss, reporting Pi_R_diff so the weighting is reproducible. The alternative (T_ref = L^2/K, giving Pi_R_diff = 1) targets quasi-steady drawdown instead and abandons the rainfall transient. State the choice in the methods section.
nondimensionalisation.revision_note: Scales corrected during Step 3.2 (2026-08-13). H_ref 30 -> 165 m and the E_ref justification rewritten; E_ref itself was already 1e8 here but nondim.py still carried the superseded 1e9. Nothing bound the two, so they had drifted in opposite directions. tests/test_scale_consistency.py now provides that binding: every difference must appear in KNOWN_DIVERGENCES with a written reason. NOTE: the groups block and diffusive_timescale below still use the earlier nondimensionalisation and have NOT been recomputed -- see the caveat.

constitutive_models.richards: mixed form: C(psi) dpsi/dt = div[K(psi) grad(psi + z)]

effective_stress.chi: chi = Se (effective saturation) in the unsaturated zone; chi = 1 when saturated
effective_stress.biot_note: alpha_B = 1.0 assumed for soft rock/soil; refine from K_solid if available

constitutive_models.bulk_density: rho_b = rho_dry + n * S_w * rho_w, with S_w = Se*(theta_s-theta_r)/n + theta_r/n
constitutive_models.porosity_update: n = n0 + eps_v,  eps_v = du/dx + dw/dz
constitutive_models.kozeny_carman: K_s = K_s0 * (n/n0)^3 * ((1-n0)/(1-n))^2  - evaluated on the same collocation points, closing the two-way coupling without outer iteration
